- F-90 **In the interpreter's library, several array and matrix declarations and `SUFFIX_SUM` are written so that the compiled checker accepts them: the default vector and matrix and `TransposedMatrix` declare the array family's bound (F-151), `__immutableFactory1` answers an `ImmutableArray1`, `__ImmutableSubArray1` has no `put`, `Matrix`'s `mul` writes its parallel halves as `do … also do … end`, and `TransposedMatrix`'s `add`, `subtract` and `negate` call `Matrix`'s operators.** `SUFFIX_SUM` loops over `seq((0 # (|x| - 1)).reverse)`, since a strided range `a:b:c` is declared `Range[\ZZ32\]`, which is no generator, so the checker refuses `seq(a:b:c)` (row 661, open). The same work built P-53 (`String`'s `left` and `right` answer `Just(c)`) and P-54 (`QQ`'s `ceiling` and `truncate` raise at the infinities and 0/0). Gated by `tests/TransposedMatrixAndFreeze.fss`; the `String` and `QQ` parts by `tests/StringPieces.fss` and `tests/NumberOrderListDeclarations.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-slips/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6.
  by: the clarity pass; note: reorganized (consolidation-2026-10-22/evidence/facts/f7/proposals.md, "F-90"); the title names the repaired declarations (rung-library-slips/REPORT.md section 1, items 1 to 6; FortressLibrary.fss:2547, :2572, :2935, :2943, :2951-2953, :4896), and says which check they pass; the bound pointed at F-151, which owns it, in place of F-94; String's left and right and QQ's rounding reduced to the decisions they build, P-53 and P-54; dropped as no longer true: __immutableFactory1's body as a site of the distance (compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv; F-264 gives its cast)
- F-220 **The compiled checker accepts `__bigOperator`'s local `body`, typed `body(i: I): L` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss`), so it is no error of the checker count (F-53).** F-228 holds how walk runs it: walk instantiates a big operator's static parameters from a declared type or the elements, not at `BottomType`. Gated under walk by `tests/UnwrittenListMapComprehensionWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md` section 6.
  by: the clarity pass; note: reorganized (consolidation-2026-10-22/evidence/facts/f7/proposals.md, "F-220"); reduced to what F-228 does not hold, the compiled checker's acceptance (FortressLibrary.fss:1316; F-53), with walk's instantiation left to F-228
- F-225 **In a self-typed trait with no `comprises` clause, or one that lists only `...`, the compiled checker types `self` in the method bodies as also the implementing type, read from the trait's F-bound; it keeps the signatures plain, and refuses an extender at another type.** It builds P-146. A self-typed trait is a trait `C[\X\]` whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`. In a trait whose `comprises` clause lists types, `self` is instead the trait met with the union of those types. For example, `object Bad extends Integral[\ZZ32\]` is refused, since `Bad` is not a `ZZ32`. The rule accepts every self-typed body of the library but `Integral`'s `numerator`, which each integer type declares instead (P-146); when it landed it cleared 29 sites of the distance, one measurement. Walk has no such rule and loads what it refuses. A compiled body that returns `self` fails verification when the parameter is an object type (row 695). The rule refuses the team demo `trips.fss`'s `generator` (row 710) and `PureList`'s `List` (row 355). Gated by `compiler_tests/SelfType*` and `XXXSelfType*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md` sections 1, 2, 4 and 7.
- F-226 **The compiled checker renames an inherited method's own static parameters apart before it uses them: from its trait's in the overloading check, and from the receiver's static arguments at a call.** So `Generator.generate[\R\]`, inherited by `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, keeps its own `R` (row 561). At a call, each method that `commonInheritedMethods` returns is instantiated with those of its own static parameters whose names the arguments mention renamed to `name$i`, the form that the checker's messages print (row 627). So a method invocation and a call by name inside a trait get the same renaming. Gated by `compiler_tests/InheritedMethodStaticParamSameName`, `InheritedMethodByNameStaticParamSameName` and `MethodStaticArgReceiverSameName`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-overloading-checker/REPORT.md` section 6 (the overloading check); `compile-ladder/rung-checker-expected-type/REPORT.md` section 1 (the call).
- F-227 **The compiled checker keeps an intersection that names a type or inference variable as written, and reads a variable below a union through the whole union or through its bound.** It expands a closed trait into its listed types only against a conjunct that names no variable (`normConjunct` and `pSubInner` in `scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala`). So a call through a parameter bounded by a closed trait and a bound that excludes a listed type checks, and the Return Type Rule accepts a valid overloading beside such a declaration (rows 686, 687, 689, 690 and 711). A `Box[\T\]` argument under a ground second bound stays refused (row 712). An overloading that the checker accepted through the expansion before this change is now refused, on a question that Appendix I lists as not settled (row 713, contested; `XXXOverloadTwoBoundsClosedTraitExclusion`). Gated by `compiler_tests/*TwoBoundsClosedTrait` and `*TwoGroundBounds*ClosedTrait`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-bounds/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6.

- F-231 **The generated AST walker is split into eight methods that the JVM compiles; as one method it ran interpreted and set the checker's time.** `Walker.walk`, which `ScalaAstGenerator` writes into `FortressAst.scala`, was one method of 31,704 bytes, past HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit for compiling a method, and the checker's substitutions and normalizations all go through it. Split in order into eight methods with identical output, on climb batch 15b's code on an idle machine, it took the count stage from 911 s to about 340 s and the distance stage from 2,375 s to 931 s. That count stage ran with the repair that lets it check a block's local functions (row 680; F-233). About 95 % of the time that remained was the solver reducing formulas again, which its memos now answer (F-235). F-240 gives the stages' times now. Gated by `WalkerJUTest`. Detail: `perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 6.
- F-232 **The syntax tree's hashes do not depend on the JVM's identity hashes, except at inference variables, walk's wrapped values and the nodes that hold them.** Every generated node's hash starts from the hash of its class's name, which makeAST's post-processing of ASTGen's output and the in-repo generators write (`build.xml:679-697`), and a field whose type holds an `Option` is hashed by `NodeHash.of` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeHash.java`), since the PLT `Option` classes hash by identity. So hash maps and sets of nodes that hold neither exception iterate in one order whatever code asked for an identity hash before, and so do the apis that `StaticChecker.checkApis` takes in turn. <!-- The FACTS clarity pass, chunk f8, 2026-10-22: F-231, F-232, F-237, F-240 and F-242 to F-245 in the clean form of proposals.md, and F-246 merged into F-259, kept as it stands, for record.py apply on a copy of the record; nothing here is applied to the real record before the coordinator checks it. -->

- F-231 **The generated AST walker is split into eight methods that the JVM compiles; as one method it ran interpreted and set the checker's time.** `Walker.walk`, which `ScalaAstGenerator` writes into `FortressAst.scala`, was one method of 31,704 bytes, past HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit for compiling a method, and the checker's substitutions and normalizations all go through it. Split in order into eight methods with identical output, on climb batch 15b's code on an idle machine, it took the count stage from 911 s to about 340 s and the distance stage from 2,375 s to 931 s. That count stage ran with the repair that lets it check a block's local functions (row 680; F-233). About 95 % of the time that remained was the solver reducing formulas again, which its memos now answer (F-235). F-240 gives the stages' times now. Gated by `WalkerJUTest`. Detail: `perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 6.
- F-232 **The syntax tree's hashes do not depend on the JVM's identity hashes, except at inference variables, walk's wrapped values and the nodes that hold them.** Every generated node's hash starts from the hash of its class's name, which makeAST's post-processing of ASTGen's output and the in-repo generators write (`build.xml:679-697`), and a field whose type holds an `Option` is hashed by `NodeHash.of` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeHash.java`), since the PLT `Option` classes hash by identity. So hash maps and sets of nodes that hold neither exception iterate in one order whatever code asked for an identity hash before, and so do the apis that `StaticChecker.checkApis` takes in turn. The exceptions: an inference variable's id is a bare `Object` (`nodes_util/NodeFactory.java:1166-1184`), but no output of the count stage moves through its hash; walk's `_WrappedFValue` hashes its value (`interpreter/evaluator/_WrappedFValue.java:170-177`; row 430). `DeclaredFunction`s still hash by identity, but since row 737's repair no choice of `ApiTypeExtractor` depends on their order (F-254). Gated by `NodeHashJUTest`, and row 737's repair by `OmittedReturnTypeFromApi`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-ast-hashes/REPORT.md` sections 4.2 to 4.4.
- F-237 **The well-formedness walk reports an ill-formed type that it meets outside the expression it is in at that expression, so a call whose static argument breaks the bound of the callee's result type is reported at the call.** A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type. An error on such a type is reported at the innermost expression the walk met it in, once for each call that made the type: the expressions that a call's value flows to share its type node and add no error, and a second call with the same printed static argument gets its own error. One exception: of two nested calls of one callee at static arguments that print alike, `next[\T\](next[\T\](x))`, only the inner call is reported (row 776). Where the type is ill-formed where it is written, its error stays at the declaration. A local variable's right-hand side is walked before the lines that use the variable, so a call whose value a variable holds is reported at the call, not at a later use. In the library, by reading, no error is added or dropped, and the distance holds no well-formedness error (F-53). Source: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala`, `check`, `error`, `outside` and `within`, and its `SLocalVarDecl` case. Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXStaticArgBoundAtCall`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtEachCall`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallNotAtUse`, `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce`, and row 776's `XXXStaticArgBoundNestedCall`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-abstract-callsite/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6, its `SKEPTIC.md` sections 5.1 and 5.2 and its `JUDGE.md`.
- F-240 **The checker's count stage takes about 63 s and its distance stage 161 s at the last landed gate, climb batch 20's.** At climb batch 15b's gate they took 325 s and 1,075 s; the solver's memos (F-235) make the difference, not load. At climb batch 20's gate the count stage ran alone after the ladder, and the distance stage beside `testFast`; the same library text took 139 s for the distance stage on an idle machine. Load can lengthen a stage more than twofold: climb batch 16's merged code took 217 s for the distance stage at its gate, at load 3.3, and nearly the same code took 574 s at load 4.6 to 5.3. So a time compares only with one taken beside like load. Source: the gate's result and `compile-ladder/climb-batch-20/gate/distance.txt`. Detail: `reviews/batch-20-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-17-review.md`, section 1; `reviews/batch-16-review.md`, section 2.
- F-242 **`SUM`'s fusion pairs with `MAX` and `MIN` hold no site of the distance: a `where` condition on each method clears their four unmet bounds, and the generic `distribute`, with its result over its own `K`, clears their two return-type errors.** The two errors were at `distribute` overloads that answer a pair over `Maybe[\T\]` beside the inherited `distribute`. With the inherited one answering `PossibleReductionPair[\K\]`, they pass the return-type rule (F-75). The team's commented text, which answers `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, only moves the two errors to the generic. The fusion stays (P-151). Row 433, fixed; F-250 gives the landing and its test. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` A.1; `perf-probes/generic-distribute/REPORT.md` sections 3 and 4.
- F-243 **The 13 sites that the where-clauses probe traced to unbuilt `where` forms, 13 of the distance's 49 errors at the gates of climb batches 15b and 16, are all cleared; the 13th, the list comparisons' site, by conditional extension.** The method condition and the generic `distribute` clear the fusion pairs' 6 (F-242), `AnyList`'s live clause its 4, with its bodies respelled within `AnyList` and none moved into `List` (F-251), and a `cast` at the identities' numeral fallback 2 (row 436). Conditional extension cleared the list comparisons' site (row 634's list half), with `ZeroIndexed[\E\]` and an element-wise `=` kept outside the condition (F-255). By the probe, library edits with no new language would also have cleared 12: dropping the fusion pairs, moving `AnyList`'s bodies into `List`, and the `cast` at the fallback. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` A.0, A.4, B.0 and B.3; `reviews/batch-17-review.md`, section 2.
- F-244 **The narrow `where` forms that the checker builds (P-151) hold where the where-clauses probe tested them; of the probe's two holes, one stands: a member checked under a conditional extension's condition stays callable where the condition fails (row 773; F-255).** A type variable opened from a `comprises` clause passes the escape, two-value and Amin–Tate tests (F-251). The other hole is closed: a method's constraint on its trait's parameter bounds that parameter inside the method and is checked at a dotted call (row 748; F-256). Swift, Rust and Haskell check the constraint at calls and scope the member to the condition. The opening of a `comprises` clause has three other open departures in the checker: rows 751, 752 and 775. F-250 (row 470) and F-256 give the constraints that the checker does not yet read. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` B.1 to B.3 and B.6.
- F-245 **Checking symbolic operators for overloading adds 186 errors to the distance in the compiled checker, measured at `d97001d19`, whose code is climb batch 20's gate: 54 clear by known library fixes, and 132 by two designs that wait for the curator.** The check was turned on in a copy of the checker whose three loops admit every operator; the checker as built skips them (row 584). The two designs are an index bound on the subscripts, with a rule for tuple indices (124 errors), and `Vector` and `Matrix` leaving `AdditiveGroup` (8) (PLAN item 59). The largest families are the subscripts over a generic `Indexed` (124) and `String`'s four (40). An earlier measurement, at `d212b2c1f`, counted 205; batches since cleared `FlatString`'s pair (F-259) and 20 of the 21 `^` errors (F-263). Walk's meet check, widened the same way in the first probe of these operators, refused only `EmptyString`'s `||`, which one declaration clears. Detail: `perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/REPORT.md` sections 0 and 1.2; `perf-probes/symbolic-operators/REPORT.md` section 1.5.
